offers_products.reason: Offerings are educational programs and degrees; no goods or software are main offerings.

offers_services.reason: Provides higher education: nursing, medical and veterinary degrees via five accredited institutions, plus employer workforce programs.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Individual students choose and enroll at Chamberlain, Walden, Ross and American University of the Caribbean.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Partners with hospitals and health systems like SSM Health and Advocate Health on workforce pipeline programs.

recurring_revenue.reason: Students pay tuition term after term across multi-year programs, giving ongoing enrollment-based revenue.

cyclical_demand.reason: Healthcare education driven by workforce shortage; enrollment tends to hold or rise in downturns, and employer partnerships are need-based.

big_ticket.reason: Degree programs (medical, nursing, veterinary) are costly, multi-year commitments chosen once by each student.

people_delivered.reason: Students pay for instruction by faculty and clinical teaching; education is delivered mainly by the institutions' staff.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are individual students at Chamberlain, Walden, Ross and AUC; health systems are partners, not the bulk.

asset_heavy.reason: Education runs on campuses, labs and partner hospital rotations; growth is driven by faculty and programs, not heavy fleets or networks.

notes: Covista is the former Adtalem Global Education; revenue mainly from student tuition, with employer partnerships secondary.
